correctness.rationale: The repaired distinct claim is the large-step P₄ witness; the multipartite parity and scalar results are retained as proved comparisons. For each even s the two top coefficients of the exact Padé polynomial satisfy a_(s,s−1)/a_(s,s)=s(s+1). Dividing at infinity gives R_s(−x)=1−2s(s+1)/x+O_s(x^−2). The constant eigenspace has multiplier exactly 1, so on the fixed path the expansion at each positive eigenvalue yields I−2s(s+1)L†/h+O_s(h^−2). Independently, path effective resistances are d_ij=|i−j| and L† is minus half the doubly centered resistance matrix. Row sums of the resistance matrix for vertices 1 and 2 are 6 and 4 and its total sum is 20, giving (L†)_12=−(1−6/4−4/4+20/16)/2=1/8. The coefficient is therefore −s(s+1)/4, strictly negative at every even s. All connected bipartite graphs on at most three vertices other than the singleton are complete bipartite; the singleton step is the identity. For the comparison, the coefficient ratios a_(s,2i)/a_(s,2i+1) increase, with a terminal unpaired even coefficient harmless in the cross-products. Thus E/O is nondecreasing and 2/(x+E(x²)/O(x²)) strictly decreases. The exact factorial-integral representation makes the numerator strictly positive for even s, and positivity of the even and odd parts gives |R_s(−x)|<1 for finite x>0. The multipartite contrast projectors yield positive off-diagonals by strict deficit monotonicity, and positive eigenvalues give positive diagonals. Odd s has graph limit 2J/n−I, while K₂ has positive entries from the strict scalar bound. No internal-stage claim is made. Frozen verify.py and its recorded exact finite checks were inspected without running it.

evidence: The s-denominator truncation of tanh(x/2) is x/D_s(x), with successive denominators 2,6,10,…,4s−2 and numerator x² at each inner level. Its error near zero is O(x^(2s+1)). The Cayley transform agrees to diagonal Padé order and has degrees at most s, so Φ_s=2/(x+D_s). The condition 0≤zF′≤F for positive finite tails in z=x² persists under F↦a+z/F, making Φ_s strictly decreasing.

value.rationale: The obstruction answers a motivated sharp-boundary question: whether unconditional positivity for arbitrarily high even orders extends to all connected bipartite meshes. P₄ is smallest possible, and a signed coefficient for the identical entry at every even order resolves the obstruction quantitatively rather than by a single low-order example or a generic existence argument. The classical scalar and multipartite results explain why this boundary is meaningful without being counted as new.
